title: The wireframe is the default look of the colony's units; the terminal holds every unit: the hostiles, the colony's machines, the eight sentries, the air and orbit, the base and the field, each on a bench
context: Owner, 2026-10-27, after the tinted wireframe test (?wire=1, entries 2026-10-26-wire-flag and 2026-10-27-wire-palette): "make the wireframe look the default, not a flag. and expand the B Bestiary to have ALL the units, including the friendlies and neutral, buildings, etc." The terminal (2026-10-14, spec docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-14-bestiary-terminal-design.md) carried the eleven hostile entries and named the friendly units and the sentries as later pages of the same screen; the owner's original brief for those was "each friendly unit as a wireframe (default) and toggleable full detail with animation diorama, each with a small lore-friendly explanation".
outcome: 1) src/td-tab.js: `wire = flags.wire !== '0'`: the sentries, the hull and the Ridgebacks are the tinted wireframe with no flag; ?wire=flat keeps the one cyan, ?wire=0 the solids (the gunship, SOL, the structures and the enemies as they were). The tracked --wire step opens without the flag and proves the default. 2) THE WHOLE TERMINAL: src/content/bestiary.js SECTIONS (hostile, colony, sentries, sky, base, field) and UNIT_ENTRIES, 36 colony entries with Isao's lines, a few facts and how each is made: the hull (the showcase's lod2), Isao (his model, Hover_Idle), the MX-06 (Walk_Cycle, at the drop's scale) and the FEIDS-26 capsule, the eight sentries through the game's own look at the top tier (src/towerlooks.js, fitted to 5 m), the KORP, SOL-82 and SOL-88, every structure the layout pins (src/content/base-layout.js STRUCTURES, at the layout's scale, its first clip looping: the Stålheart's Terraforming_Cycle, the foundry's, the radar's Array_Slew, the assembly's) plus the gate, the back gate and the scoreboard, and the field's neutral things (the life container and the shell rack through units.js builders, a deployed Hugin, the wreck, the DAY 42 ball). src/domain/bestiary.js terminalRoster (the hostiles first, then the colony by section, one numbering), unitState (`needs`: always / a programme perk / an unlocked sentry / the four landed / a sector reached / the SOL-88 launch / the party; the lab's host opens all), unitCard. src/fx/unit-bench.js: one unit at the stage's centre at its true size on the 6 m rings, drawn as the game draws it (setWireframe tinted), its clip looping, a late load dropped by token; src/fx/bestiary-stage.js mode 'unit' with the camera orbiting the unit's box (BESTIARY_BENCH.orbit), eased from the disc's view as the unit lands; src/fx/terminal-screen.js: the section heads in the list, the facts block on the card (a sentry's cost and top-tier rows from src/towers.js), Enter or Space swaps WIRE / SOLID on a colony entry (the footer says so), the locked note for an entry the run has not reached, host.world() from td-tab's terminalWorld() (the perks, the unlocked sentries, the landing, the sector, the launch, the party). The terminal opens on the first open entry, now the hull. 47 entries; on the finished base with the four landed 22 are open (the launcher, SOL-88, the ball, the Needle and the Heptapod wait for their signals).
alternatives: The Units lab's carousel as the friendly page: a second renderer and a second screen; the owner asked for the one terminal, and the bench is the lab's turntable under the terminal's CRT.
A fixed unit scale on the bench: the camera fits the box instead, so the shell rack and the Stålheart both fill the frame and the rings give the size.
Friendly entries always open: the run's progress is the point of the terminal (met / not met), so a colony entry opens on the signal that brings the thing into the run.
evidence: npm test 309 (new test/bestiary-units.mjs: the roster order and numbering, every need known and every model on disk, each need opened by its signal, the card's two shapes), npm run check (td-tab 5,347 under 5,450), npm run architecture green.

--bestiary-units PASS (new): no flag, the hull wired by default (mode tint); B after the landing: 47 entries, 22 open, the ball locked, the hostiles unseen, the colony after the hostiles; the Rotor on the bench 12/12 meshes wired, box r 2.5 (5 m), three facts rows, the WIRE / SOLID footer; Enter -> 0/12 wired; the MX-06 38/38 with Walk_Cycle; the Stålheart 10/10 with Terraforming_Cycle at r 25.3; the ball's card locked with its note; a hostile's footer back to PACK 3/6; the lab: 47 full, the KORP and a Heptapod (70/70) on the bench. --bestiary: its expectations moved to the hostile section (the terminal now opens on the hull; the always-open entries are full before any contact; the states are computed at the first open): bestiary-unseen and bestiary-white PASS, then the step fails on its stalk check (every body REST at phase 0 for 30 s), and the base commit f4b7f6b3 fails on the same check in a worktree: stale since the glide (the DAY 42 record), not this work.
